lesson_title: Headlights On: Budgets and the Art of Writing the Future Down
hook_text: Same lathe. Same R9 000. One workshop sailed through, one watched the rent bounce. The difference? A page.
clip_script: Two workshop owners buy the same R9 000 wood lathe. The first sits down in September and writes the future: October in, October out — purse grows to R8 000. November: the lathe lands, the purse dips to R4 000 — thin, but it holds, ON PAPER, before a rand moves. She buys in November, the dip arrives exactly as written, December recovers to R9 000. The second owner buys on a good feeling, in a lean month, and watches the rent debit bounce. Same machine. Same price. The difference was never the money — it was the LOOKING AHEAD. That page is a cash budget: money coming in, money going out, and the balance that survives, written BEFORE it happens. Every statement you have ever drawn is a rear-view mirror — it shows the past. A budget is the headlights. And here's the twist: your family already writes one every month-end at the kitchen table. Same tool a whole city uses. Just fewer zeros.
visual_style: Split-screen of two workshop owners: one writing months onto a glowing forward calendar with a purse level tracking each column, the other's purse crashing on an impulse buy; ending on headlight beams lighting a dark road of months.
mood: Cautionary then empowering — planning as a quiet superpower.
pacing: Parallel storytelling beats, converging on the headlights metaphor.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write next month before it happens.
